title: GPT-6 Models Demonstrate Intrinsic Wet-Lab Protein Design via Reasoning & Code
whyItMatters: Shows general-purpose frontier reasoning models can design functional wet-lab protein binders and predict molecular docking using reasoning and code—surpassing specialized models like DiffDock.
summary: In a November 24, 2026 preprint and wet-lab collaboration with Onava, OpenAI demonstrated that general-purpose GPT-6 reasoning models possess intrinsic protein-design capabilities using natural-language reasoning and code alone. Across 322 lab-tested minibinders against five protein targets, 35 bound their targets (10.9% hit rate across all five targets), while 66–70% of redesigned antibody/VHH binding loops retained target binding. On blind and covalent small-molecule docking benchmarks, GPT-6.2 and an internal model achieved 92–97% accuracy versus 50–60% for DiffDock.
technicalHighlights: Wet-lab verified with Onava: 35 of 322 GPT-6.2-designed minibinders bound targets across all 5 tested proteins; 70% of 182 VHH and 66% of 272 therapeutic antibody loop redesigns retained binding.
Reached 93–96% blind docking accuracy (vs. 50% for DiffDock-L) and 92–97% covalent docking accuracy on the Scarpino dataset (vs. 60% for DiffDock).
Demonstrated prompt-steerable structural motif scaffolding via explicit physics/chemistry reasoning and code rather than bespoke structural diffusion weights.
caveats: Preprint not yet peer-reviewed. OpenAI candidly notes that specialized models (ProteinMPNN, ESMFold) still assisted sequence selection/filtering in the wet-lab workflow, and de novo structure prediction from raw sequence remains a weakness.

scoreRationale.foundational: Signals a paradigm shift where general-purpose reasoning LLMs rival or outperform specialized structural-biology models.
scoreRationale.ripple: Lowers the barrier to programmable therapeutic binder and antibody engineering through natural-language prompting.
scoreRationale.verification: Backed by physical wet-lab binding assays across five targets with Onava, though still at preprint stage and partially assisted by specialized sequence tools.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed multi-model computational protein engineering pipelines into promptable reasoning-and-code loops.
